report.root_cause: Deploy OPS-260 (deploy/2026-11-01-statscache.md) pushed plugins/StatsCache/config.yml at 08:28:41 changing retain-history from false to true. The StatsCache plugin hot-reloaded it at 08:28:42 and began retaining session-history entries in memory without bound: heap climbed ~5 MB/s (361 MB -> 740 MB of 768 MB), reaching 1200 entries / ~343 MB held. TPS stayed at 20; no player or world impact.
report.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs at shift start (healthy). 2) Observed heap 361->540->653 MB over ~60 s with no entity/chunk change; correlated with log line '[StatsCache] config reloaded (retain-history=true)' at 08:28:42, config.yml mtime 08:28:41, and deploy note OPS-260. 3) Read deploy/previous/StatsCache-config.yml (retain-history: false). 4) Declared incident. 5) Wrote plugins/StatsCache/config.yml back to retain-history: false / history-size: 1000 (identical to previous deploy value); plugin hot-reloaded it at 08:29:42 and growth stopped, but heap stayed pinned ~740 MB because already-retained entries were not released. 6) Found /statscache <stats|flush>; 'statscache stats' showed 1200 entries ~343.3 MB; ran 'statscache flush' which freed ~343.3 MB. 7) Verified: heap fell to 305 MB, 'statscache stats' reports 0 entries / 0 MB (retain-history=false); watched ~140 s more — heap sawtooths normally (374->444->360 MB with GC), TPS 20, both players stayed online. No restart, no bans, no deletions.
report.residual_risk: The OPS-260 change (keep session history in memory for the weekly stats report) is now reverted, so that feature is not active; the ticket owner needs a different approach (e.g. bounded/on-disk history or a larger heap) before re-enabling retain-history, since the plugin evidently does not honour history-size (1200 entries > 1000 configured) and will leak again if re-enabled. The deploy note deploy/2026-11-01-statscache.md was left in place and still describes the now-reverted change. Heap max is 768 MB which is tight for this plugin set.
